description: Machine-readable inventory of architecture audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence to a soft check.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete code or configuration breaks the invariant.

enrichmentFlags.description: Declare the intended architectural pattern (layered, feature-folders, hexagonal) so boundary checks judge against the stated intent.

relatedAudits.relationship: Builds the knowledge graph the boundary and coupling checks read from.
Owns component-level design; state and data-flow checks overlap.

checks.title: No circular dependencies
checks.violationSignal: One or more cycles are detected by the knowledge graph; each cycle is reported as an ordered list of module paths.

checks.title: Feature folders have a single entry point
checks.expectation: Each top-level feature or module folder exposes a barrel index.ts and external imports go through it.
checks.violationSignal: An external file imports from a deep path inside a feature folder, bypassing its index.ts.

checks.title: No deep relative imports
checks.expectation: Relative imports go up at most two levels (../../).
checks.violationSignal: Any import string containing ../../../ or deeper.

checks.title: No back-imports across layers
checks.expectation: In a layered pattern, upstream layers do not import from downstream layers; in a feature-folder pattern, sibling features import only through their public entry points.
checks.violationSignal: An import that crosses a boundary in the wrong direction, reported with importer, import, and direction.

checks.title: Cross-workspace contracts respected
checks.expectation: Internal packages import only from each other's published entry points, not deep paths.
checks.violationSignal: A deep import into another workspace's src/ directory.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The project is not a monorepo.

checks.title: No god module
checks.expectation: No single module has fan-in greater than the threshold.
checks.violationSignal: A module exceeds the threshold, reported with its path, rank, and inbound edge count.

checks.title: No god component
checks.expectation: No React component is rendered by more than the threshold number of parents.
checks.violationSignal: A component exceeds the threshold, reported with its path and the count of distinct rendering parents.

checks.title: File size budget
checks.expectation: No source file exceeds the threshold in lines.
checks.violationSignal: A file exceeds the threshold, reported with its line count.

checks.title: Component fan-out budget
checks.expectation: No component imports more than the threshold number of modules.
checks.violationSignal: A component exceeds the threshold, reported with the count and the imported modules.

checks.title: No orphaned files
checks.expectation: Every source file is reachable from at least one entry point.
checks.violationSignal: Files with zero inbound edges that are not themselves entry points, reported as likely-dead modules for the user to verify.

checks.title: Single state-management strategy
checks.expectation: Exactly one global state strategy is used, not multiple in the same application.
checks.violationSignal: Two or more state-management libraries are present with no declared migration path.

checks.title: Data fetching layer separated
checks.expectation: Server state lives in a designated data-fetching layer, not in component-level useEffect plus fetch.
checks.violationSignal: Files outside the designated hooks or data layer call fetch, axios, or framework data primitives directly.

checks.title: No global mutable singletons
checks.expectation: No top-level let exports hold mutable state.
checks.violationSignal: A module-level mutable export such as export let x = ...

checks.title: Side effects isolated
checks.expectation: Components go through a hook or service module rather than reading or writing localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie, or window.* directly.
checks.violationSignal: Direct usage of those browser globals in component files.

checks.title: Server vs. client distinction
checks.expectation: The 'use client' directive is used deliberately, and server and client components do not import each other's exclusive modules.
checks.violationSignal: A 'use client' file importing a server-only module, a server component importing a client-only one, or more than half of components marked client.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The Next.js App Router is not in use.

checks.title: File-naming consistency
checks.expectation: Files match the dominant naming pattern in their directory.
checks.violationSignal: Files whose name does not match the dominant pattern in their directory.

checks.title: Directory-structure consistency
checks.expectation: Every directory at the same depth follows the same organisational convention as siblings of the same kind.
checks.violationSignal: A directory that does not match the inferred pattern for its kind.

checks.title: Index barrels consistent
checks.expectation: If barrel files are used in any feature folder, they are used in every feature folder.
checks.violationSignal: Mixed-mode barrel usage across feature folders.

checks.title: Public API documented
checks.expectation: Each feature folder's index.ts has a documenting comment block, or the folder has a README.md.
checks.violationSignal: Feature folders without either a documenting barrel comment or a README.md.
